title: Moving Contract Red Flags & Hidden Fees in Addis Ababa
excerpt: Spot bad moving quotes in Addis: vague scope, cash-only demands, surprise stair fees, and standby charges—what to insist on in writing before move day.
content:
Why contracts matter in Addis

Moving disputes here rarely go to court—they end at the compound gate with a truck half-loaded. A one-page written scope prevents “that was not included” arguments when stairs, standby time, or extra trips appear. Professional movers itemize; brokers often do not.

Red flags before you pay

  • No company name or phone on the quote—only a personal mobile.
  • 100% cash upfront with no receipt or contract reference.
  • Price per “trip” without truck size or crew count.
  • Refusal to visit or video survey for anything beyond a few boxes.
  • “We are cheapest” without listing stairs, packing, or fuel assumptions.

Hidden fees to clarify in writing

  • Stair carry or long push from gate (common in condos and Lebu villas).
  • Elevator booking fees paid to management—who pays?
  • Standby when security delays entry—hourly jobs suffer most.
  • Extra trip because truck was too small—should be caught at survey.
  • Packing materials billed per box without prior estimate.

What a fair quote includes

Truck class, crew size, hours or fixed total, disassembly scope, blanket use, and payment schedule (deposit vs balance on completion). Compare with published starts on our cost guide—if a quote is far below with no survey, assume missing line items.

Delala brokers vs direct movers

Middlemen sometimes subcontract to the lowest bidder day-of. Ask who operates the truck and whether the crew works for Active Movers or a partner—see delala vs professional.

If you already signed something vague

Stop payment on disputed extras; photograph inventory and access issues; call the supervisor listed on the contract. For office moves, involve building management in writing.

Book with clear terms

Written quote request · Hourly vs fixed · +251982260000

Phrases that should make you pause

  • “Pay the rest when we finish unloading” with no signed total beforehand.
  • “Stairs are extra” mentioned only when the truck is loaded.
  • “We need a bigger truck” without showing why at survey.
  • “Fuel is separate today” on a quote that claimed all-inclusive.

Change orders done right

True scope changes—extra storage stop, attic volume discovered—need a signed amend before work continues. That is how Active Movers handles additions; see price creep prevention.

Condo-specific traps

Brokers quote low assuming passenger elevators; management then blocks load. Confirm freight lift rules in writing and tie them to the quote—condo checklist.

Reliability cross-check

Operators who refuse line items often refuse accountability—what makes a mover reliable.

Sample fair clause

“Price includes 3-ton truck, four movers, blankets, standard disassembly, one origin and one destination with freight lift slots booked by client. Additional stops or volume over survey require signed change order.” If your quote cannot say something this plain, keep shopping.
